verdict.rationale: Bun's package manager is documented as an npm-compatible drop-in replacement for npm, yarn and pnpm that works in any Node.js project. It pulls packages from the npm registry, tarball URLs and git, with `bun add` and global installs, and `bun info` reads registry metadata (bun-docs-26, bun-docs-31, bun-docs-54, bun-docs-5, bun-docs-49). A community comment confirms it can be adopted purely as a package manager at near-zero switching cost (bun-comm-3). Missing for 10: independent hands-on evidence that installs succeed across the breadth of the registry, including native addons (node-gyp support is only a commenter's belief, and Windows install crashes are reported); lifecycle scripts are blocked by default, so packages that need postinstall require manual `trustedDependencies` entries.
